findings.title: Queues are unbounded, so the new strategy provides no backpressure
findings.body: FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit() always enqueues and returns successfully, never raising MessageRejected. Despite the class docstring claiming natural backpressure, Arroyo will keep consuming from Kafka while workers fall behind, accumulating messages and WorkItem/result objects in memory indefinitely when one queue is slow or stuck, risking OOM instead of pausing consumption.

findings.title: Closing a strategy permanently kills the shared queue pool that the factory reuses
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()/terminate() calls queue_pool.shutdown(), which shuts down the queues and workers. That pool is created once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and reused by create_thread_queue_parallel_worker() on every create_with_partitions() call (e.g. after a Kafka rebalance, when Arroyo closes the old strategy and creates a new one for the new assignment). Submits to the now-shutdown queues raise queue.ShutDown, which submit() catches at line 317 and then marks the offset complete, so messages for the new assignment can be committed without ever being processed. The factory only clears queue_pool in its own shutdown(), not when a strategy is closed.

findings.title: Failed work items are marked complete and their offsets are committed
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker.run() logs any exception from result_processor but unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset() in the finally block, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit() similarly marks offsets complete when decoding/grouping/enqueueing fails. The commit loop then treats those offsets as processed and commits them, contradicting the documented 'Only commits offsets after successful processing' guarantee: transient processing failures or poison messages are silently dropped and will not be redelivered.

findings.title: Kafka offsets are committed from a background thread instead of the Arroyo processor thread
findings.body: _commit_loop runs on its own thread and invokes commit_function, which in result_consumer.py calls Arroyo's Commit callable. Arroyo strategies are expected to invoke commit from the strategy's submit/poll/close calls on the StreamProcessor thread; calling it concurrently from this thread races StreamProcessor's own offset/assignment handling and can commit offsets against a stale or revoked assignment. Additionally, each strategy instance created for a rebalance spawns another commit thread over the same shared OffsetTracker, so two threads can race get_committable_offsets()/mark_committed() and double-commit.

findings.title: close() stops the commit loop before draining queues, discarding commit progress
findings.body: close() sets shutdown_event and joins the commit thread before calling queue_pool.shutdown() to drain pending work. Workers then finish processing queued items and mark offsets complete, but no commit loop remains to commit those offsets and close() performs no final commit flush. On every graceful shutdown/rebalance, all work completed during the drain is therefore reprocessed on restart, causing duplicate result processing.

findings.title: Offset scan is O(offset range) every second while a queue is blocked
findings.body: get_committable_offsets() iterates range(start, max_offset + 1) for every partition on every 1-second commit loop iteration. The strategy's stated purpose is to survive a slow item blocking a queue; in exactly that case all later offsets accumulate in all_offsets/outstanding, so each poll rescans an ever-growing range (quadratic overall) and the sets grow without bound for as long as one offset is stuck, wasting CPU and memory.

findings.title: OffsetTracker is never reset when partitions are revoked or reassigned
findings.body: OffsetTracker keeps all_offsets, outstanding and last_committed forever, with no hook to clear a partition when Arroyo revokes it or when create_with_partitions is called with a new assignment. Stale outstanding offsets from a previous assignment block commits for a reassigned partition, and if offsets restart below the stale last_committed value (consumer-group reset, topic recreation, or reassignment with an earlier starting offset from the partitions mapping, which the strategy ignores), get_committable_offsets() can never advance past last_committed and commits silently stall.
